title: Alt-Bindings in Keyboard Manager bugged after windows update
author: sssssy

status.label: Alt-remap regression is specific enough
status.detail: The issue isolates a first-press failure after Alt release, and current Keyboard Manager engine code already has special Alt and WM_SYSKEYDOWN handling that needs direct replay.

next_action.label: Reproduce Alt-first-press remap regression
next_action.reason: Identify which Alt modifier-state branch is leaking through after recent Windows updates before proposing a fix.

judgment.rationale: The report cleanly isolates a specific Alt-only regression: the first Alt-based shortcut remap after releasing Alt emits the original Alt+key instead of the remapped target, while later presses work until Alt is released again. Current Keyboard Manager engine code has explicit AltGr and WM_SYSKEYDOWN modifier-state handling, so the right next step is a controlled maintainer replay on a current build.
evidence: The issue says Alt-based remaps fail on the first press after Alt is released, then start working on subsequent presses.
The report says the same mappings work correctly when Ctrl or Shift is used instead of Alt.
The issue associates the change with a recent Windows update, making current-build replay important.
Current Keyboard Manager engine code contains dedicated AltGr and WM_SYSKEYDOWN state-handling branches in KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp.
judgment.recommended_action: Replay the exact Alt-remap scenario on a current build and inspect the Alt modifier-state transitions before choosing a code path.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix may be needed, but the current evidence does not yet prove which Alt-specific state path regressed after the reported Windows update.

issue_context.summary: Alt-based Keyboard Manager remaps miss the first chord after Alt is released, while analogous Ctrl and Shift remaps continue to work.
known_information: The issue targets Keyboard Manager on PowerToys 0.100.2.
The repro uses Alt-hjkl style remaps to cursor keys.
The first Alt-based press after releasing Alt emits the original Alt+key instead of the remapped result, but repeated presses work until Alt is released again.
The reporter ties the behavior to a recent Windows update.
inferences: The problem is likely in Alt modifier-state tracking rather than in the generalized remap pipeline, because Ctrl and Shift variants still work.
The regression may involve a change in how Windows emits Alt key-down/key-up or WM_SYSKEYDOWN events after the update.
issue_context.analysis: The report is already specific enough to move to maintainer reproduction. Current engine code has special-case Alt state handling, but the artifact should stop at a reproduce action until a current replay identifies the exact branch that misfires.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body, labels, and timeline.
Inspected KeyboardManagerEngineLibrary/KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp around AltGr tracking and WM_SYSKEYDOWN handling.
Checked for assignees, attachments, and linked fixes; none were present.

reproduce.title: Verify first Alt-remap press after Alt release
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.100.2 or current main on a machine with the reported Windows update behavior
prerequisites: Alt-based shortcut remaps such as Alt+H/J/K/L configured
setup: Prepare a simple text or cursor-target application where the original Alt+key behavior is visible.
steps: Press an Alt-based remapped shortcut once after Alt has been fully released.
Observe whether the first press emits the original Alt+key instead of the remapped target.
Repeat the same shortcut again without fully resetting Alt state and compare the second press.
Repeat with a Ctrl-based or Shift-based equivalent to confirm the issue is Alt-specific.
reproduce.expected_result: Every Alt-based remap press should produce the remapped target immediately, including the first press after Alt is released.
